title: Summarize the commitment before payment entry
trigger: The payment form collects card details before the buyer can see the complete selected offer.
action: Place a concise order summary beside the payment step: plan, quantity, currency, actual charge, recurrence, and verified trial or discount terms. Refresh it from the authoritative checkout state whenever the order changes.
mechanism: A visible commitment reduces uncertainty immediately before a consequential action.
guardrail: Use actual billing values, including known taxes and mandatory charges; distinguish estimates from final totals.
measure: Completed first payments; billing-confusion contacts and refunds.

title: Allow order edits without restarting checkout
trigger: A buyer discovers the wrong plan or seat count after reaching payment and must restart the entire journey.
action: Provide an edit-order route that retains the authenticated buyer and permitted non-sensitive billing details. Return to checkout with a refreshed provider-backed summary and the corrected selection.
mechanism: Reversibility can reduce fear of committing to an accidental choice.
guardrail: Invalidate stale sessions or amounts as needed and prevent multiple active checkouts from creating duplicate purchases.
measure: Recovered checkout completion; wrong-plan purchases.

title: Keep checkout quantity and payment synchronized
trigger: Changing checkout quantity updates the visible subtotal but leaves a stale final total or provider payment session.
action: Validate quantity against the catalog rules, then update the summary and payment state together. Explain invalid quantities explicitly and prevent older asynchronous responses from replacing the latest intended order.
mechanism: A consistent response makes editing the purchase feel controlled and avoids surprise at confirmation.
guardrail: Revalidate quantity and final amount server-side; handle rapid edits, minimums, unavailable quantities, and stale checkout sessions.
measure: Completed correctly sized purchases; stale-total and quantity disputes.

title: Show discount acceptance and renewal consequences
trigger: A buyer applies a code but cannot tell whether it worked or how long the reduced price lasts.
action: Display the accepted discount, affected billing periods, final charge, and verified price afterward. Give a precise rejection reason for invalid or ineligible codes without clearing the rest of checkout.
mechanism: Feedback resolves uncertainty about receiving the expected offer.
guardrail: Validate eligibility and stacking server-side; do not display a discount before the provider accepts it.
measure: Completed discounted purchases; renewal-price complaints.

title: Resolve tax uncertainty before the final action
trigger: The first tax-inclusive amount appears only after the buyer has committed or repeatedly changes without explanation.
action: Collect only the location or tax information the existing checkout needs, then show the calculated tax and payable total before confirmation. Explain when an amount remains an estimate and update it when required fields change.
mechanism: Earlier cost clarity can reduce last-moment surprise and mistrust.
guardrail: Use the provider's supported tax calculation; do not make jurisdictional assumptions or promise exemptions.
measure: Checkout completion; total-price disputes and calculation errors.

title: Keep optional coupon entry unobtrusive
trigger: A prominent empty coupon box encourages ready buyers to leave checkout searching for a discount.
action: Place optional code entry behind a clearly labeled 'Have a code?' disclosure while keeping it accessible. Leave validated campaign codes applied and visible in the summary rather than making buyers retype them.
mechanism: Removing an unnecessary search cue may help buyers complete the offer they already chose.
guardrail: Do not conceal an available earned discount or make legitimate codes difficult to use.
measure: Completed purchases; code-entry failures and discount support requests.

title: Offer supported payment methods buyers can use
trigger: Qualified customers abandon because the sole displayed method is unavailable or inconvenient in their market.
action: Use evidence about the actual audience to surface supported wallets or local payment methods through the existing provider. Keep an appropriate fallback and explain any method-specific subscription limitation before selection.
mechanism: A familiar usable payment method can reduce both effort and uncertainty.
guardrail: Verify recurring-payment support, currency, fees, and fulfillment timing before enabling a method.
measure: Paid completion by eligible method; failures and contribution after fees.

title: Turn declines into specific recovery paths
trigger: A failed payment produces only 'Something went wrong' or invites endless retries with the same card.
action: Map provider-safe decline categories to useful next actions, such as checking details, contacting the issuer, authenticating, or using another method. Preserve the order and make the current charge status explicit.
mechanism: An actionable explanation can prevent a recoverable payment failure from becoming abandonment.
guardrail: Do not expose sensitive fraud signals or retry beyond supported provider rules.
measure: Recovered payments; repeated declines and duplicate-charge complaints.

title: Restore checkout after bank authentication
trigger: Buyers complete additional bank authentication but return to an empty page or lose the selected order.
action: Persist the validated checkout identity through the provider's authentication flow and restore an accurate success, pending, or failure state on return. Offer a safe status refresh if the response is delayed.
mechanism: Continuity reduces the uncertainty created by leaving the site's interface.
guardrail: Handle canceled and expired authentication; verify the provider state instead of trusting redirect parameters.
measure: Authenticated payment completion; abandoned or duplicated attempts.

title: Explain asynchronous payment without false failure
trigger: A supported payment method remains pending while the site treats the absence of immediate confirmation as a decline.
action: Show a distinct pending state with the expected next step, a truthful status check, and the actual access policy. Explain whether the buyer should wait or complete another required action.
mechanism: A legible waiting state can prevent unnecessary retries and fear that money disappeared.
guardrail: Never promise a completion time without evidence or grant paid entitlement from a pending client redirect.
measure: Confirmed payments after pending; duplicate attempts and support contacts.

title: Make repeated payment clicks harmless
trigger: Slow responses cause buyers to click the final payment action several times.
action: Show a responsive submitting state and use the existing server/provider idempotency mechanism for repeated requests. If the connection times out, reconcile the first attempt before offering another charge attempt.
mechanism: Immediate feedback and reliable retry behavior can preserve trust during an uncertain moment.
guardrail: A disabled button alone is insufficient; verify retries, refreshes, duplicate webhooks, and concurrent tabs.
measure: Completed unique purchases; duplicate charges and timeout abandonment.

title: Confirm the receiving account or workspace
trigger: A person manages several workspaces and could buy for the wrong one.
action: Show the workspace or account receiving the subscription before payment and let an authorized buyer change it through the proper context switch. Carry that identity into checkout creation and fulfillment.
mechanism: A concrete destination reduces the risk of purchasing something that cannot be used where intended.
guardrail: Validate workspace membership and billing authority server-side; avoid leaking other tenants' details.
measure: Correctly assigned purchases; transfer requests and unauthorized billing.

title: Prevent accidental second subscriptions
trigger: An existing subscriber reaches a public purchase link that could create another subscription for the same need.
action: Recognize the current entitlement and route the buyer to the actual change-plan or additional-workspace flow. Explain when a second purchase is genuinely separate instead of silently treating every click as a new sale.
mechanism: Protecting an existing commitment can reduce costly surprise and preserve future trust.
guardrail: Do not block legitimate multi-workspace purchases; verify authoritative subscription state rather than stale UI flags.
measure: Appropriate upgrades and new purchases; accidental duplicates and refunds.

title: Keep transaction currency unmistakable
trigger: A checkout uses an ambiguous currency symbol or changes currency between the site and payment provider.
action: Display the actual transaction currency beside the final amount, preserve the intended supported currency through checkout, and explain any conversion handled outside the merchant's charge. Use local formatting without changing the underlying amount.
mechanism: A clear monetary unit can remove uncertainty about the real commitment.
guardrail: Do not promise issuer exchange rates or fees; reconcile provider currency and amount in the receipt.
measure: International paid completion; currency disputes and mismatched charges.

title: Collect invoice details at the relevant moment
trigger: Business buyers need an invoice in their organization's name but cannot provide or correct billing details during purchase.
action: Provide an optional business-billing section with the fields the provider actually supports, showing how they will appear on the invoice. Permit safe correction before confirmation without requiring unrelated profile information.
mechanism: Making the purchase administratively usable can reduce hesitation from business buyers.
guardrail: Verify required tax identifiers and invoice rules through the existing provider; avoid unsupported tax advice.
measure: Completed business purchases; invoice correction requests.

title: Resume a deliberately interrupted checkout
trigger: A buyer returns after closing or canceling hosted checkout and must reconstruct the order.
action: Offer a resumable summary of the validated selection, current availability, and charge. Reuse or recreate the provider session safely, explicitly resolving changed prices or expired offers before proceeding.
mechanism: Preserved context can reduce the effort of returning to an earlier intention.
guardrail: Never silently revive an expired promotion or charge through an old authorization without a new deliberate action.
measure: Resumed purchases; stale-offer and duplicate-session incidents.

title: Preview the real effect of a plan change
trigger: An existing subscriber sees a full plan price but cannot tell what will be charged or credited now.
action: Retrieve the provider-supported change preview and show the immediate financial effect, effective date, and next renewal before confirmation. Distinguish a plan comparison price from the actual change transaction.
mechanism: A concrete preview can reduce uncertainty about changing an ongoing commitment.
guardrail: Do not reproduce proration from rounded UI prices; verify the preview matches the transaction applied.
measure: Completed appropriate changes; proration disputes and unwanted upgrades.

title: Provision paid access despite a lost redirect
trigger: Payment succeeds but the buyer closes the checkout tab before returning, leaving access unavailable.
action: Fulfill from verified server-side payment state and make the account reconcile its entitlement when reopened. Show a useful status-recovery action rather than asking the customer to purchase again.
mechanism: Reliable delivery protects the confidence created by paying and makes the purchase usable.
guardrail: Verify signatures, deduplicate events, and handle event ordering through the established provider integration.
measure: Paid accounts reaching first value; paid-but-locked support cases.

title: Distinguish cancellation from failed payment
trigger: Returning from hosted checkout displays an alarming error even when the buyer deliberately canceled without paying.
action: Show an accurate canceled-checkout state, retain the editable offer, and provide a normal route back to the product or plans. Reserve failure language for an actual failed attempt.
mechanism: Respecting a deliberate pause can keep the buyer willing to return.
guardrail: Reconcile provider state before saying no payment occurred, particularly after interrupted or asynchronous attempts.
measure: Later completed purchases; false-failure and charge-status confusion.

title: Give payment support a safe context reference
trigger: A buyer cannot resolve a checkout problem and support must ask them to repeat the entire story.
action: Offer a support route containing a non-sensitive checkout reference and a concise description of the current state. Let the buyer choose to contact support and explain what information is useful to share.
mechanism: A reachable recovery path can reduce uncertainty when self-service fails.
guardrail: Never include card data, payment secrets, or unnecessary personal details in links or analytics; do not send a message automatically.
measure: Recovered purchases; resolution time and sensitive-data exposure.
